tagline: A loop from Duncan Hines's front door, river ferry included.
intro: The tour starts at Duncan Hines's old home on US 31W in Bowling Green and heads north on KY 101 into Edmonson County, by Rhoda and Huff to Sunfish and Bee Spring, then into Mammoth Cave National Park and over the Green River on the ferry. It comes back by Sloans Crossing, Smiths Grove and Oakland, 83 miles around.

Hines sold printing for a Chicago firm and had eaten many meals on the road by 1935, when he and his wife Florence turned their list of good restaurants into a book, Adventures in Good Eating. The cake mixes came later, after he sold the rights to his name, from a mill company that licensed it.

moments.title: Kyrock
moments.text: A company town that quarried rock asphalt and shipped it by steamboat on the Nolin and Green rivers to pave roads, and gave up its charter in 1966 after the company closed.

moments.title: Green River Ferry
moments.text: Running since 1934, the last river ferry in Mammoth Cave National Park carries cars, hikers and bikers across the Green River 364 days a year.

moments.title: Pig
moments.text: The name was argued over until a resident mentioned a small hog he had seen on the road, and Pig it was.
